problems.detail: The 制/伏 positive pairing reads 「時珍曰伏水制雌黄熖消」 and is glossed 'subdues water'. The BCGM 卷13 苦參 氣味 note actually reads 伏汞 (subdues MERCURY): verified against the 本草綱目/草之二 text on zh.wikisource.org, which gives 「時珍曰：伏汞，製雌黃、焰硝。」 汞 has been reduced to 水, turning a named mineral drug into a nonsense object. Same class of defect as the H142 辰丹砂 glyph corruption. The error is inherited (harvest_verification_results.json carries 伏水 once, in the H214 classical_contraindications allySays string), so the upstream harvest string must be corrected too, not just the re-filing. Classification itself is now RIGHT: this attempt moved 伏/制 into positive pairings, where the earlier pass had it in drug_incompatibilities with relation 'other' (safety_field_decomposition.json, H214 record 1).

陳藏器's 「生者墮胎」 is parked in unclassified as 'direction uncertain'. The verified harvest disagrees: harvest_verification_results.json, H139 classical_contraindications (verdict VERIFIED) counts it as one of 'Three contraindications: 張元素…; 朱震亨…; 陳藏器「生者墮胎」'. A pregnancy signal the verified record graded as a contraindication now reaches NO safety field. Not silently dropped (it is escalated with a reason), but it must not load in this state; two sources disagree and a human has to rule.

Same pattern as H139: 「杀蛔堕胎」 (本草備要 1694) is parked in unclassified as direction-uncertain, while the verified harvest records it under the heading 'PREGNANCY: Wang Ang, 本草備要 1694, states it classically' (harvest_verification_results.json, H253 classical_contraindications, VERIFIED). The two caveats given are both sound (simplified-glyph transcription; BCGM assigns 墮胎 to the ROOT not the seed), but as filed the pregnancy signal reaches no safety field. 延胡索 H271 「通經堕胎」 is parked the same way, so this is a three-herb pattern in this slice, not a one-off.

「蒸食消酒毒」 (陳藏器, BCGM 主治) is filed in positive_pairings with relation 解毒. It sits inside a 主治 run, the same sentence as 生者墮胎 and 可斷穀不飢作粉尤妙, so it is an INDICATION (steamed and eaten it dispels wine toxin in the drinker), not a 七情 drug relation. This is the exact distinction the same attempt drew correctly for H214's 殺䖝 ('an indication, not a 殺 drug-relation') and for H253's 杀蛔. Filing it as a relation creates a pairing row implying 酒 is a partner drug. Harmless in direction (it can never surface as a warning), but inconsistent with the attempt's own stated rule.

drug_incompatibilities contains 「之才曰惡𤣥參蛇蛻皮」 TWICE, byte-identical, same speaker, within a single record. The filed set should be three rows (BCGM 之才; 本草從新 惡元參; 神農本草經 七情表 惡蛇蛻、元參), not four. Content and relation tagging are correct; de-duplication defect only.

Same de-duplication defect: 「之才曰畏海蛤文蛤」 appears twice, byte-identical, within a single record, alongside the 1799 七情表 witness. Likely upstream, since the harvest verifier already flagged the H284 claims file for carrying a duplicated [CONTRA] line (harvest_verification_results.json, H284, verdict PARTLY_VERIFIED). Check the dedupe step rather than patching the two rows by hand.

Two INCOMPAT rows are composite quotes tagged with a single relation 反, and one of them carries a POSITIVE envoy inside drug_incompatibilities. Row: 反神農本草經 七情 appendix (1799)「栝蔞　枸杞為使；惡干薑；畏牛膝、乾漆；反烏頭。」 — 枸杞為使 (goji is its envoy) is a 使 relation and renders, from the incompatibility field, as though goji were a drug to avoid. Same shape in 反吳儀洛 (本草從新 1757, 栝蒌仁)「畏牛膝、乾漆。惡乾薑。反乌頭。」, which is filed under 反 although it states 畏 and 惡 relations too — the relation-collapse shape that produced the H142 defect in the first attempt, though here no glyph is corrupted and every individual relation is also filed correctly on its own row from the BCGM witness. Fix: split both composites by relation verb and route 枸杞為使 to envoy_pairings (where the 1799 envoy is in fact already filed separately).

INCOMPAT carries the reciprocal aconite entry verbatim as a gua lou incompatibility row: 反神農本草經 七情 appendix (1799)「烏頭、烏喙　莽草為使，反半夏、栝蔞、貝母、白蘞、白芨」. Only the 栝蔞 token in that line concerns this herb. As filed, the row imports 莽草為使 (aconite's envoy, a positive relation) plus 半夏、貝母、白蘞、白芨 — four substances that are aconite's antagonists, not Trichosanthes', into Trichosanthes' incompatibility list. The verifier cited this line as corroboration of 反烏頭 (harvest_verification_results.json, H283 classical_contraindications: 'Independently corroborated twice… and the reciprocal entry'), i.e. it is evidence, not a pairing of this herb's own. Fix: keep it as a corroboration/provenance note on the 反烏頭 row, not as a standalone incompatibility row.

The BCGM 1596 adulterant-toxicity warning for 茜草 is absent from all five buckets, including unclassified: 「勿用赤柳草根，真相似，只是味酸濇，誤服令人患内障眼，速服甘草水止之，即毒氣散」 (recorded in eastern_qc_pre1900_results.json, H206, 'ADULTERANT WARNING (BCGM 1596)') — a red-willow root looks identical, and taking it by mistake causes cataract, to be checked at once with licorice water. This is a stated 勿用 prohibition with a named harm, and it is exactly the category this same pass DID file for H169 (the 野菊/苦薏 adulterant clauses, filed as clinical with an identity/adulterant scope tag). One rule has to apply to both. Note the 忌鐵 / 勿犯鉛鐵氣 metal-contact rules for this herb are correctly excluded as preparation doctrine, consistent with H256's stated policy; this clause is not preparation doctrine.

INCOMPAT row 畏吳儀洛 (本草從新 1757)「畏萆。」 is a truncated drug name — 萆 alone is not a substance; the relation is 畏萆薢, as the BCGM row directly above it in the same bucket correctly gives (之才「畏萆薢」). This is now much improved on the first attempt: the string is attributed to its witness, and the verifier confirms the 本草從新 transcription itself prints 「畏萆。」 (harvest_verification_results.json, H281 classical_contraindications), so nothing was introduced by this pass. But if the row loads as-is it names no real substance and will not match any lookup key. Fix: footnote it as the 1757 transcription's truncation of 萆薢 rather than shipping a bare 萆. Related and now correctly handled: the 3-item 「惡乾薑、白蔹、芫花。」 vs the 4-item BCGM/1799 lists (missing 藜蘆) is a genuine source difference and is now labelled with its witness, which is what the earlier audit asked for.

Two CLINICAL rows are drinking-manner rules rather than patient-state prohibitions: 藏器曰「飲之宜熱冷則聚痰」 (drink it hot; drunk cold it gathers phlegm) and 李廷飛曰「大抵飲茶宜熱宜少不飲尤佳空腹最忌」 (drink it hot, drink it little, better not at all, worst on an empty stomach). The verifier files both under 'PREPARATION DOCTRINE — a temperature-management rule, not a processing rule' (eastern_qc_pre1900_results.json, H160), and the adjacent food clause from the same source run, 胡洽「與榧同食令人身重」, was routed to DIETARY. Same run, adjacent clauses, different buckets. This is the SAFE direction of the error (a manner rule shown as clinical, not a real prohibition demoted to diet), and 空腹 is arguably a patient state, so this is defensible rather than clearly wrong — but it is the one item the first attempt's own log flagged here that has not moved. Note the genuinely clinical rows in the same bucket (虚寒/血弱, 大渴及酒後, 服威靈仙土茯苓者) are correctly placed.

POSITIVE carries 殺神農本草經 七情 appendix (1799)「殺天雄、附子毒」 — two drugs. The project's other internal witness gives three: eastern_qc_pre1900_results.json (H268) records the 之才 line as 「殺天雄附子烏頭毒」, adding 烏頭. The filed two-drug form matches the 1799 string verbatim as transcribed by the verifier (harvest_verification_results.json, H268: 「遠志　得茯苓、冬葵子、龍骨，良；殺天雄、附子毒；畏珍珠、蜚蠊、藜蘆。」), and the BCGM 卷12下 之才 line contains no 殺 clause at all, so the filing follows the stronger evidence and nothing is inverted — this is a positive antidotal relation either way. Flagging only so the two internal files are reconciled before load rather than silently picked between.

The one 制 (positive, toxicity-restraining) pairing this herb has is filed in no bucket, not even unclassified: BCGM 1596 發明「近醫毎以緑豆同用治病有效，葢豆寒椒熱，隂陽配合得宜，且以豆制椒毒也」 — physicians pair black pepper with mung bean, the bean being cold and the pepper hot, so the bean restrains the pepper's toxin (eastern_qc_pre1900_results.json, H107, 'PREPARATION DOCTRINE … an explicit toxicity-restraint pairing'). Parallel 制/伏 relations were filed to POSITIVE elsewhere in this same slice (H092 制雄黄, H182 伏硫黄, H206 汁制雄黄, H282 伏砒), so the omission is an inconsistency rather than a policy. No safety inversion — the effect is only that a mitigating pairing is missing.

The 辰丹砂 defect is NOT fixed, only diluted. INCOMPAT still carries the BCGM row 惡之才曰「惡葱實辰丹砂牡丹藜蘆」 filed under the single verb 惡, with 辰 still absorbed into the substance string and no footnote saying it is the corrupt/illegible 畏 of the Siku transcription. A customer-facing list renders 「辰丹砂」 as though it were a drug (Chen-prefecture cinnabar). This pass DID add the corrective witnesses (1799 七情表 split as 惡蔥實 + 畏丹砂、牡丹、藜蘆, and 1757 畏丹皮、丹砂), which is an improvement over the previous attempt, but the two are left unreconciled: 牡丹 and 藜蘆 now appear under 惡 in one row and 畏 in another for the same herb, and nothing tells the loader which verb is correct. Verified against harvest_verification_results.json H142 pairings row, which states the 1799 table 「黃芩　山茱萸，龍骨為使；惡蔥實；畏丹砂、牡丹、藜蘆。」 splits exactly where the stray 辰 sits. Fix: keep the BCGM string verbatim but tag 辰 as the illegible verb and mark the row as superseded on relation type by the 1799 witness.

The Lei Xiao 御風草 co-use prohibition 「凡使天麻勿用御風草…若同用令人有腸結之患」 has been moved OUT of drug_incompatibilities into unclassified. It is the single most safety-load-bearing clause tian ma has: a named substance pair with a named harm (腸結, intestinal blockage), verified verbatim in harvest_verification_results.json (H274, classical_contraindications, VERIFIED). The record's stated reason is that the relation enum admits only 畏/惡/反 — but the previous pass filed this same clause inside drug_incompatibilities with relation 'other' (safety_field_decomposition.json, H274), so the field demonstrably can carry it. Direction here is genuinely negative, unlike the 勝/解毒 cases that were correctly moved to positive, so parking it in unclassified is not the same fix. If unclassified does not load, a real prohibition disappears. Fix: restore to drug_incompatibilities with an explicit non-七情 relation type, or extend the enum.

CLINICAL carries the 附方 line 「咽乾乃虚中有熱不可服涼藥…」 as a second contraindication record. That line restricts COOLING DRUGS (涼藥) inside the 欬膿血 formula; it is not a restriction on 黃耆, which is warm. The record's own annotation concedes it is 'NOT a standalone herb-level contraindication', yet it sits in the contraindication bucket anyway, where a mechanical loader will publish 'dry throat means heat within deficiency, do not take cooling medicines' as an astragalus contraindication. The verifier's note (harvest_verification_results.json, H002) endorses it only as context, not as a contraindication. Contrast H175, where the analogous formula-scoped line genuinely restricts a chen-pi-containing formula and so belongs where it is. Fix: move to unclassified, or add a hard formula-scope field that suppresses it from the herb-level warning render.

The fourth INCOMPAT row is malformed: it is typed 反, attributed to 吳儀洛 1757, and then bundles the 1799 七情 appendix inside the same row quoting 「丹參　畏鹹水，反藜蘆。」 followed by a second quote 「反藜蘆。」. One row therefore carries two independent witnesses and two different relations (畏 and 反). Consequence: the 1799 witness of 畏鹹水 is not filed as its own 畏 row, and a row typed 反 displays a 畏 relation inside its quoted text. No content is lost and no direction is inverted, so this is presentation only, but it should be split into separate per-witness, per-relation rows before load (compare the clean four-row structure this same herb had in the previous pass).

The p.94 record is filed whole into clinical_contraindications as 「…無甚感鬱之人藉以充潤腸胃當亦小有資補若傷冒時疫以此橫塞中焦羸尪雜症妄冀蘇起沉疴未覩其益必蒙其害世有良工其察鄙言」. Only the span 若傷冒時疫…必蒙其害 is a prohibition. The leading clause 無甚感鬱之人藉以充潤腸胃當亦小有資補 is a qualified POSITIVE indication (for a patient without much stagnation it fills and moistens the intestines and stomach and gives small supplementing benefit) and belongs in unclassified, kept adjacent to the contraindication it is contrasted with; the trailing 世有良工其察鄙言 is a rhetorical address to practitioners with no clinical content. As filed, any renderer that shows clinical_contraindications, and especially any that truncates, leads with a benefit statement under a contraindication heading, which inverts direction for that clause. Nothing is lost: all three spans are present verbatim and the record's own gloss states the contrast correctly, so this is misfiling, not a dropped clause. Note the same pass DID split the parallel p.93 run, correctly routing 山西通志謂黨參今無產者 to unclassified while keeping 舉世以代神草…胸滿氣隔之患 clinical, so the two records are handled inconsistently. Fix: keep 若傷冒時疫…必蒙其害 as the clinical text and move the opening positive clause and the closing rhetorical clause to unclassified with a pointer back to the contraindication. Consequence of the current state: unclassified holds 1 entry where the slice expects 3.

unclassified: 附方 (formula section) 「痔瘡腫痛{{SK notes|連翹煎湯熏洗後以刀上飛過緑礬入麝香貼之　集騐方}}」 — REASON: this is a treatment formula for haemorrhoid swelling and pain (fumigate/wash with Lianqiao decoction, then apply levigated green vitriol with musk), i.e. an indication plus its co-ingredients. It is not a warning of any kind and must not be filed as one. Recorded here only so that no clause from the verified text is dropped. Scope: this one 附方 only, not the drug as such.

items.herb: Perilla Leaf (Zi Su Ye, 紫蘇)

clinical_contraindications.text: 機曰宋仁宗命翰林院定湯飲奏曰紫蘇熟水第一以其能下胸膈浮氣也盖不知其久則泄人真氣焉
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 機曰 Wang Ji (汪機), quoted in BCGM 卷十四 發明, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Wang Ji: Emperor Renzong of Song had the Hanlin Academy rank medicinal drinks and perilla hot-water was placed first, because it can bring down floating qi in the chest and diaphragm. What they did not realise is that over the long term it drains a person's true qi. — A prolonged-use caution.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug, prolonged/habitual use as a daily beverage

clinical_contraindications.text: 宗奭曰紫蘇其氣香其味微辛甘能散今人朝暮飲紫蘇湯甚無益醫家謂芳草致豪貴之{{SKchar2|927}}者此有一焉若脾胃寒人多致滑泄往往不覺
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 宗奭曰 Kou Zongshi, quoted in BCGM 卷十四 發明, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Kou Zongshi: perilla is aromatic, faintly pungent-sweet, and dispersing. People who drink perilla decoction morning and night gain nothing by it; physicians speak of aromatic herbs bringing on the diseases of the rich and noble, and this is one of them. In people with a COLD SPLEEN AND STOMACH it frequently causes slippery diarrhoea, often without their noticing. TEXTUAL NOTE: the character shown as 疾 in some transcriptions is a lacuna here ({{SKchar2|927}}); 疾 is a standard restoration, not printed text in this SKQS recension.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; patient state = cold spleen and stomach 脾胃寒人

clinical_contraindications.text: 氣虚表虚者禁之。（俗喜其芳香、旦暮恣食、不知泄真元之氣、古稱芳草致豪贵之疾、此類是也。）
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin (吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo), 1757
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Prohibited in those with qi deficiency or exterior deficiency. (Common folk delight in its fragrance and indulge in it morning and evening, not knowing that it drains the true original qi; the ancients' phrase about aromatic herbs bringing on the diseases of the rich and noble is exactly this sort of thing.) Here 疾 IS printed.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; patient state = 氣虚 / 表虚

clinical_contraindications.text: 多服泄人真气
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草備要 Ben Cao Bei Yao (汪昂 Wang Ang), 1694
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Taken in excess it drains a person's true qi. A dose/duration caution.

clinical_contraindications.text: 蘇子…腸滑氣虚者禁之
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin (吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo), 1757
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Perilla SEED: prohibited in those with slippery intestines (loose stool) or qi deficiency.
clinical_contraindications.scope: the seed 蘇子 only, NOT the leaf or stem

clinical_contraindications.text: 表弱气虚者忌用叶，肠滑气虚者忌用子
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草備要 Ben Cao Bei Yao (汪昂 Wang Ang), 1694
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Those with a weak exterior or qi deficiency must avoid the LEAF; those with slippery intestines or qi deficiency must avoid the SEED. NOTE: the 忌 here is followed by a patient state plus a plant part, so it is CLINICAL, not dietary. The split-by-part rule is correctly attributed to BCBY 1694.
clinical_contraindications.scope: part-specific — leaf 叶 vs seed 子, stated as two separate rules

dietary_avoidances.text: {{SK anchor|莖葉氣味辛温無毒}}{{SK notes|李廷飛曰不可同鯉魚食生毒瘡}}
dietary_avoidances.speaker: 李廷飛曰 Li Tingfei, quoted in BCGM 卷十四 莖葉氣味 note, 1596
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Stem and leaf: pungent, warm, non-toxic. Li Tingfei: must not be eaten together with CARP (鯉魚), it produces poisonous sores. Tang/Song food-combining lore, not a clinical prohibition.

dietary_avoidances.speaker: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin (吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo), 1757
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Avoid carp. 忌 here is followed by a FOOD, therefore dietary, not clinical.

dietary_avoidances.speaker: 本草備要 Ben Cao Bei Yao (汪昂 Wang Ang), 1694 (simplified-character transcription)
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Avoid carp. Same dietary rule as BCCX, carried independently by BCBY.

positive_pairings.speaker: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin (吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo), 1757
positive_pairings.gloss: The more aromatic the better. It SUITS / is well paired with tangerine peel (橘皮). This is a recommended combination, a positive instruction — it must never render as a warning.

positive_pairings.speaker: 本草備要 Ben Cao Bei Yao (汪昂 Wang Ang), 1694 (simplified-character transcription)
positive_pairings.gloss: The more aromatic the better. It suits tangerine peel. BCBY carries the identical pair 宜橘皮/忌鲤鱼 as BCCX.

unclassified: BCGM 卷十四 莖葉 「氣味辛温無毒」 and 主治 「下氣除寒中其子尤良{{别録}}」 with 時珍's 「解肌發表散風寒行氣寛中…」; seed 「子氣味辛温無毒主治下氣除寒温中{{SK notes|别錄}}」 — REASON: nature/flavour and 主治 (indications). Conditions being TREATED, not caused. Not a warning in any bucket.

本草從新 1757 「蘇梗（宣、順氣。）順氣安胎。功力稍緩、挟虚者宜之。」 — REASON: indication for the STEM (蘇梗). 安胎 = calms/secures the fetus and 挟虚者宜之 = suitable for those with concomitant deficiency. Both are positive indications. IMPORTANT: 安胎 must not be inverted into a pregnancy contraindication; the stem is here recommended in pregnancy.

本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin (吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo), 1757
本草備要 Ben Cao Bei Yao (汪昂 Wang Ang), 1694

unclassified: VERIFIED ABSENCE, independently confirmed in two pre-1900 works. Dutt 1877 p.156 (BAUHINIA VARIEGATA; Sans. Kanchanara, Kovidara; Hind. Kachnar) gives 「the properties of both are said to be identical. The bark of Bauhinia variegata is described as alterative, tonic, astringent and useful in scrofula, skin diseases and ulcers」 followed by Chakradatta's and Sarangadhara's formulae (Kanchanara guggulu) — no caution anywhere. Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica vol.1, 1890, gives Bhavaprakasa properties, Concan usage and the Makhzan's account (astringent, attenuant, tonic; checks diarrhoea, removes worms) — indications throughout, no restriction. REASON: everything present is an indication; nothing in either work reads as a contraindication, dietary avoidance, incompatibility or pairing.
sourcesUsed: U. C. Dutt, The Materia Medica of the Hindus, 1877
Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica, vol. 1, 1890

clinical_contraindications.text: 但性稍寒。無火者勿服。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin 卷五草部 (吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo), 1757
clinical_contraindications.gloss: But its nature is somewhat cold. Those WITHOUT FIRE (i.e. lacking a heat/fire pattern) must not take it. A patient-state prohibition.

unclassified: Surrounding entry text 「甘微苦寒。除心熱。平肝風。舒筋除眩。下氣宽中。…主肝風相火之病。風静火息。則諸證自平。（相火散行於胆、三焦、心包。）祛肝風而不燥。庶幾中和。故小兒科珍之。…有刺類钓钩。故名。」 — REASON: nature/flavour, indications (clears heart heat, calms liver wind, relaxes sinews, stops dizziness), mechanism and name etymology. Conditions being TREATED, not caused.
RETRIEVAL NOTE (not a clause): the Wikisource transcription of Ben Cao Cong Xin uses simplified 钩藤; searching only traditional 鉤藤/釣藤 returns nothing. That is a retrieval trap, not an absence.
sourcesUsed: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin 卷五, 吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo, 1757

unclassified: VERIFIED ABSENCE. No entry for 猴頭 exists in the Shennong Bencao Jing (Sun Xingyan recension, 1799), in the Bencao Gangmu 1596 fungus class (卷28 菜之五 芝栭類, fifteen named kinds, none of them Hericium), or in Ben Cao Cong Xin 1757. With no entry there is no contraindication line to quote, and reporting the absence is the correct result. clinical_contraindications.text: 宗奭曰芍藥須用單葉紅花者為佳然氣虚寒人禁之古人云減芍藥以避中寒誠不可忽

clinical_contraindications.gloss: Kou Zongshi: for peony one should use the single-petalled red-flowered kind, which is best; however it is PROHIBITED in people with qi deficiency and cold. The ancients said 'reduce the peony to avoid cold in the centre' — this truly must not be neglected.

It MUST NOT BE USED POSTPARTUM, because its sourness and coldness attack the generating and upbearing qi. If it is absolutely unavoidable, use it stir-fried in wine. clinical_contraindications.text: …熱生風濕生虫故又能治風殺䖝惟腎水弱而相火勝者用之相宜若火衰精冷真元不足及年高之人不可用也

clinical_contraindications.gloss: Heat generates wind and damp generates worms, hence it can also treat wind and kill worms. It is suitable ONLY for those whose kidney water is weak and whose ministerial fire is excessive. If the fire is declining, the essence cold, the true original qi insufficient, OR THE PERSON IS ADVANCED IN YEARS (及年高之人), it MUST NOT BE USED. The 及年高之人 limb is part of the verbatim text and must not be trimmed.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; patient states = declining fire / cold essence / insufficient true original qi / advanced age

clinical_contraindications.text: 久服黄連苦参而反熱者…氣增不已則臟氣有偏勝…故有暴夭

clinical_contraindications.gloss: Those who take Coptis and Kushen over a long period and paradoxically develop heat… when the qi is increased without cease, the organ qi becomes one-sidedly dominant… hence there are sudden untimely deaths. clinical_contraindications.text: 肝腎虚而無熱者忌。（其氣能傷腎、沈括梦溪笔談云：久用苦參擦牙、逐病腰痛、由其氣傷腎也。）

clinical_contraindications.gloss: Avoid in those with liver and kidney deficiency and no heat. (Its qi can injure the kidneys; Shen Kuo's Mengxi Bitan records that prolonged use of Kushen as a tooth-rub brought on lumbar pain, because its qi injures the kidneys.) 忌 here is followed by a PATIENT STATE, so clinical, not dietary.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; patient state = 肝腎虚而無熱

clinical_contraindications.text: …令人能食。大便燥结。因寒筋急。勿用。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin 卷十二 (吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo), 1757
clinical_contraindications.gloss: …it makes a person able to eat. In DRY, BOUND STOOL (大便燥结) and in SINEW TENSION ARISING FROM COLD (因寒筋急), DO NOT USE (勿用). Two distinct patient states under one prohibition.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; patient states = 大便燥结 and 因寒筋急

clinical_contraindications.text: 宗奭曰薏苡仁本經云微寒主筋急拘攣…故可用薏苡若素問言因寒則筋急者不可更用此也…
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 宗奭曰 Kou Zongshi, quoted in BCGM 卷二十三 發明, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Kou Zongshi: the Bencao Jing says Coix is slightly cold and governs sinew tension and cramping… so Coix may be used [where the tension is from heat/damp]; but where the Suwen speaks of sinew tension arising FROM COLD, this must not be used further. Attribution to 寇宗奭 confirmed.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; patient state = 因寒則筋急 (cold-caused sinew tension)

unclassified: 本草備要 1694 (汪昂 Wang Ang): 「…薏苡去湿要药，因寒因热，皆可用也。《衍义》云∶因寒筋急者不可用，恐不然」 — REASON: this is an explicit DISSENT, not a prohibition. Wang Ang states Coix is a key damp-dispelling drug usable whether the cause is cold or heat, and that the Bencao Yanyi's 因寒筋急者不可用 is, he suspects, not so. Filing it as a contraindication would reverse its meaning; filing it as a pairing would be wrong too. Loader should surface it as a countervailing classical opinion against the two 因寒筋急 contraindications above.

本草備要 1694 closing line: 「杀蛔堕胎」 (within 「但其力和缓，用之须倍于他药。杀蛔堕胎，炒熟微研。」) — REASON: DIRECTION CANNOT BE SETTLED from the text as given. 杀蛔 (kills roundworm) is an anthelmintic ACTION against a parasite, not a 七情 drug relation, so it does not belong in positive_pairings. 堕胎 sits in the same list-of-actions register and could read either as an abortifacient use (a capability) or as a pregnancy hazard (a warning); per the direction rule it is left here rather than guessed. TWO CAVEATS THE LOADER MUST CARRY: (a) the only reachable text is a SIMPLIFIED-character Wikisource transcription, so traditional 殺蛔墮胎 has NOT been confirmed against a woodblock scan — treat as a lead, not a citation; (b) BCGM assigns 墮胎 to the ROOT, not the seed — 卷二十三 根: 「煮服墮胎{{SK notes|藏器}}」, attributed to 陳藏器, and there it sits in a 主治 context meaning the root is USED to induce abortion. The classical abortifacient evidence for the SEED therefore rests on 本草備要 alone.

本草從新 1757 and 本草備要 1694: 「其力和緩。用之須倍於他藥。炒熟微研。」 / 「但其力和缓，用之须倍于他药。…炒熟微研。」 — REASON: DOSAGE and PROCESSING instructions (its power is mild and moderate, so use double the amount of other drugs; stir-fry until done and grind lightly). Not a warning in any of the four buckets.

TRANSCRIPTION CAUTION, carried forward from the verified record: the 本草備要 text available is a simplified-character Wikisource transcription with dropped glyphs. All BCBY strings above should be re-checked against a traditional woodblock witness before customer-facing publication.

unclassified: 「爲活血利氣之藥」 — reason: statement of function (a blood-quickening, qi-freeing medicine). Indication/action, not a warning of any kind.
「然辛溫走而不守。」 — reason: nature/flavour characterisation (acrid, warm; it moves and does not hold). Rationale for the cautions rather than a prohibition in itself.

「通經堕胎。」 — reason: DIRECTION UNCERTAIN. Appears inside a run of function statements, not clearly in a 主治 list and not clearly a warning. It may read either as a capability (frees the menses, brings down a fetus) or as a caution against use in pregnancy. Per the direction rule this must not be guessed; flagged for a human reading of the surrounding 本草從新 column.

「瘀滞有餘者宜之。」 — reason: positive indication (suitable for those with excess stasis and stagnation). The inverse of a contraindication, but it names no partner drug, so it is not a positive pairing either.

「生用破血。炒用調血。（酒炒行血、醋炒止血。）」 — reason: 修治/炮製 processing doctrine (raw breaks blood; dry-fried regulates blood; wine-fried moves blood; vinegar-fried stops bleeding). Preparation instruction, not a contraindication, not a food, not a 七情 relation.

drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Xu Zhicai: it fears / is diminished by Hai Ge 海蛤 (clam shell). First of two drugs in this single 畏 clause; split so neither is lost. Full source string: 「之才曰畏海蛤文蛤」.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 = Xu Zhicai
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Xu Zhicai: it fears / is diminished by Wen Ge 文蛤 (a second clam shell drug). Second of two drugs in the same 畏 clause. Full source string: 「之才曰畏海蛤文蛤」.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 神農本草經 孫星衍輯本, 1799, 七情表
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Ze Xie fears Hai Ge and Wen Ge. Independent 1799 witness to the same 畏 pair.

unclassified: 「宗奭曰…本草引扁鵲云多服病人眼誠為行去其水也」 (寇宗奭 Kou Zongshi, BCGM 發明) — reason: commentary EXPLAINING the Bian Que eye caution (it is truly because the drug drives off the body's water). Explanatory gloss on a clause already filed, not an additional prohibition.

「好古曰本經云久服明目扁鵲云多服昏目何也」 (王好古 Wang Haogu, BCGM 發明) — reason: Wang Haogu poses the contradiction rather than resolving it — the Ben Jing says prolonged use brightens the eyes, Bian Que says heavy use dims them. It is a question about the tradition, not a directive, so it cannot be filed as a contraindication in either direction.

dietary_avoidances.text: 忌諸血無鱗魚蘿蔔蒜葱
dietary_avoidances.speaker: 時珍曰 = Li Shizhen (BCGM 氣味 note)
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Li Shizhen: avoid all blood 諸血, scaleless fish 無鱗魚, radish 蘿蔔, garlic 蒜, and scallion 葱. Five items, enumerated so none is lost. The full 忌 string in the source runs 「忌諸血無鱗魚蘿蔔蒜葱鐵器」; the sixth item 鐵器 (iron vessels) is not a food and is filed separately under unclassified.

dietary_avoidances.text: 忌猪肉血羊血無鱗魚觸藥無力
dietary_avoidances.speaker: 何首烏傳, quoted in BCGM 集解
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Avoid pork and pig's blood 猪肉血, sheep's blood 羊血, and scaleless fish 無鱗魚; contact with them renders the medicine powerless 觸藥無力. Three food items plus the stated consequence. Attached to the He Shou Wu Zhuan's course of administration, not stated as a standing herb-level rule by Li Shizhen himself.
dietary_avoidances.scope: the 何首烏傳 dosing regimen quoted in 集解, i.e. for the duration of that course of taking the drug — not stated as a drug-level rule

positive_pairings.speaker: 時珍曰 = Li Shizhen
positive_pairings.gloss: Li Shizhen: Fu Ling 茯苓 (poria) acts as its ENVOY (為之使) — a guiding partner. Positive combining instruction, not a warning.

positive_pairings.speaker: 時珍曰 = Li Shizhen (same BCGM 氣味 note)
positive_pairings.gloss: Together with Di Huang 于(干/乾)地黄 it can SUBDUE cinnabar 硃砂 (伏硃砂). 伏 is a positive control relation — the pair masters cinnabar's toxicity. This must never be rendered as 'do not combine with cinnabar'; the source says the opposite. 于 is the transcribed glyph and is preserved as harvested (read as 干/乾, dried Rehmannia).

unclassified: 「鐵器」 (tail item of Li Shizhen's 忌 list, full string 「忌諸血無鱗魚蘿蔔蒜葱鐵器」) — reason: iron vessels are equipment, not a food, not a patient state, and not a 七情 drug relation. It is a preparation/handling avoidance and belongs in whatever field carries processing instructions; filing it as a dietary avoidance would misdescribe it and filing it as an incompatibility would be worse. Explicitly retained so it is not lost with the food items it was bundled with.
「氣味苦濇微溫無毒」 — reason: taste/nature/toxicity header (bitter, astringent, slightly warm, non-toxic). Not a warning; the 無毒 is a safety statement, not a prohibition.

「凡服用偶日二四六八日服訖以衣覆汗出導引尤良」 (何首烏傳, in BCGM 集解) — reason: dosing schedule and aftercare regimen (take on even days, 2/4/6/8; after taking, cover with clothing to sweat; daoyin exercise is especially good). Administration doctrine, not a contraindication. Carried because it is the clause the dietary 忌 list is attached to.

clinical_contraindications.text: 元素曰升陽生津脾虚作渴者非此不除勿多用恐傷胃氣
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 元素曰 = Zhang Yuansu
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Zhang Yuansu: it raises yang and engenders fluids — for thirst from spleen deficiency nothing else will remove it — BUT do not use much, for fear of damaging stomach qi (勿多用恐傷胃氣). The prohibition is on quantity, not on the herb outright; the first half of the same clause is an indication and is noted so the whole string stays intact.

clinical_contraindications.text: 震亨曰凡㿀痘已見紅㸃不可用葛根升麻湯恐表虚反増㿀爛也
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 震亨曰 = Zhu Zhenheng
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Zhu Zhenheng: whenever pox 㿀痘 has already shown red spots, Ge Gen Sheng Ma Tang may NOT be used, for fear the exterior is made deficient and the pox instead worsens and ulcerates. Note the prohibition is stated against the named formula, not against the single herb.
clinical_contraindications.scope: the formula 葛根升麻湯, in the specific patient state of pox already showing red spots — a formula-level and stage-specific prohibition, not a herb-level one

clinical_contraindications.text: 上盛下虛之人。雖有脾胃病。亦不宜服。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛) 卷五, 1757 — unattributed within the work
clinical_contraindications.gloss: A person with repletion above and deficiency below should not take it, even if they do have a spleen-stomach illness. Genuine patient-state prohibition.

clinical_contraindications.text: 即當用者，亦宜少用。多則反傷胃氣。以其升散太過也。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛) 卷五, 1757 — unattributed within the work
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Even those for whom it IS indicated should use little; much of it will instead damage stomach qi, because its raising and dissipating action is excessive. A dosage limit. FLAGGED: the harvester dropped this qualifier from the submitted fragment — it is restored here.

clinical_contraindications.text: （夏月表虛汗多、尤忌。）
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛) 卷五, 1757 — parenthetical gloss in the work
clinical_contraindications.gloss: In summer months, with exterior deficiency and profuse sweating, it is especially to be avoided. 忌 here governs a PATIENT STATE, not a food, so this is clinical and not dietary.

positive_pairings.speaker: 藏器 = Chen Cangqi (BCGM 主治)
positive_pairings.gloss: Steamed and eaten, it DISPELS alcohol toxin 消酒毒. An antidote capability, the same shape as 解…毒 — the herb acts beneficially on another substance's toxicity. It is not a prohibition and must never be rendered as 'do not combine with alcohol'. Appears within the 主治 list, so it is an indication as well as a capability.

unclassified: 「生者墮胎」 (藏器 Chen Cangqi, BCGM 主治) — reason: DIRECTION UNCERTAIN by rule. 墮胎 sits inside a 主治 (indications) list, where the convention is that a term names something the drug is used FOR — i.e. the raw root is used to bring down a fetus. Read that way it is a therapeutic action, not a warning. It cannot be filed as a contraindication without inverting the 主治 convention, and it cannot be filed as a plain indication without risking a real pregnancy-safety signal being buried. Escalated rather than guessed.

「可斷穀不飢作粉尤妙」 (藏器 Chen Cangqi, BCGM 主治) — reason: famine-food / grain-abstention use (it can replace grain so one does not hunger; made into a powder it is especially fine). A dietary USE, the opposite of a dietary avoidance; no prohibition present.

「升陽生津脾虚作渴者非此不除」 (元素 Zhang Yuansu) — reason: the indication half of the Zhang Yuansu clause. Retained separately for visibility; the clause as a whole is already filed under clinical_contraindications for its 勿多用恐傷胃氣 tail, and is not being double-counted as a warning.

「久服，強魂、聰明、輕身、不老，通神明」 (神農本草經 孫星衍輯本, 1799) — reason: benefit claim for prolonged use (strengthens the hun, sharpens hearing and sight, lightens the body, prevents ageing, frees the shen-ming). Indication, not a warning. Carried so the whole of the 1799 entry is accounted for.

dietary_avoidances.text: 惟和麫作䬪飥則動氣為不能制麫毒也
dietary_avoidances.speaker: 詵曰 = Meng Shen (孟詵), BCGM 卷二十七 發明
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Meng Shen: ONLY when it is mixed with wheat flour 麫 and made into botuo 䬪飥 (a boiled noodle/dough dish) does it stir qi 動氣 — because it cannot control wheat's toxin 為不能制麫毒也. IMPORTANT READING: the phrase contains 制…毒, but it is NEGATED (為不能制 = 'because it is unable to control'). This is the REASON for the avoidance, not a positive control claim. It must not be filed as a 制伏 pairing.
dietary_avoidances.scope: whole drug, but only in the specific combination with wheat flour

dietary_avoidances.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛), 1757, 山藥 — unattributed within the work
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Do not eat it together with wheat/noodles. The 1757 restatement of Meng Shen's wheat-flour avoidance, in plain imperative form. Kept as its own record because it is a separate witness in a separate work.
dietary_avoidances.scope: whole drug, in combination with wheat

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 = Xu Zhicai, BCGM 卷二十七 根氣味 note
positive_pairings.gloss: Xu Zhicai: Zi Zhi 紫芝 (purple reishi) acts as its ENVOY (爲之使) — a guiding partner directing the formula. Positive instruction. Extracted from the same string that also carries the 惡甘遂 antagonism.

positive_pairings.speaker: 神農本草經 孫星衍輯本, 1799, 七情表
positive_pairings.gloss: Shu Yu: Zi Zhi 紫芝 serves as envoy. Second witness to the same positive envoy relation, from the 1799 七情 table.

unclassified: 「利丈夫助隂力」 (詵曰 = 孟詵, BCGM 發明) — reason: indication/benefit claim (benefits men, aids yin power). Not a warning.

「熟煮和蜜或爲湯煎或爲粉並佳乾之入藥更妙」 (詵曰 = 孟詵, BCGM 發明) — reason: preparation doctrine (cook it through with honey, or as a decoction, or as a powder — all fine; dried for medicinal use is finer still). Processing instruction, not a contraindication. Carried because it is the clause the wheat-flour avoidance is contrasted against (惟… = 'only when…').

「色白而堅者佳。（形圓者、爲西山藥、形扁者、爲怀山藥…）」 (本草從新, 1757) — reason: quality selection and provenance/variety note (white and firm is best; round-form = Xi Shan Yao, flat-form = Huai Shan Yao). 怀 is a simplified glyph for 懷, preserved as harvested. Neither warning nor pairing.

「普曰神農甘小温桐君雷公甘凉無毒」 (普曰 = 吳普 Wu Pu, citing 神農, 桐君 and 雷公, BCGM) — reason: competing taste/nature attributions (Shennong: sweet, slightly warm; Tong Jun and Lei Gong: sweet, cool, non-toxic). Materia-medica header data, not a warning.
「二月、八月采根」 (吳普 gloss, 神農本草經 孫星衍輯本, 1799) — reason: harvest timing for the root. Split off from the parenthesis whose other half (惡甘遂) is filed as an incompatibility, so that neither half is lost.

drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Fears / is diminished by Bei Mu (Fritillaria), Da Huang (rhubarb), Tu Si Zi (Cuscuta seed).

positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Gou Qi as envoy, recorded under the seed.

unclassified: 畏惡同栝蒌。 (吳儀洛, 本草從新 1757, 天花粉 entry) — cross-reference, not a stated pairing: 'its 畏 and 惡 relations are the same as those of 栝蒌'. Names no drug of its own and spans TWO relations at once (畏 and 惡), so it cannot be filed under a single relation value. Resolves in practice to 畏牛膝、乾漆 and 惡乾薑 as listed above, now attached to the root as well as the seed.

通乳消腫。治结胸胸痹。酒黃熱痢。二便不通。炒香酒服。止一切血。 (吳儀洛, 本草從新 1757, 栝蒌仁) — 主治 INDICATIONS plus a preparation note, i.e. conditions TREATED, not caused. Retained here so the run is demonstrably not dropped; it precedes 「寒胃滑腸…勿投」 in the same sentence block, which is why the prohibition must be cut off from it deliberately.

腫毒發背。乳痈瘡痔。 … 即栝蒌根。澄粉食。大宜虚熱人。 (吳儀洛, 本草從新 1757, 天花粉) — 主治 indications, an identity gloss (天花粉 = the 栝蒌 root) and a positive suitability statement ('very suitable for people with deficiency-heat'). Not warnings. Recorded so that the only prohibition in that entry, 「脾胃虚寒者。均宜戒用。」, is seen to have been extracted from surrounding indication text rather than the whole block being filed as a warning.
sourcesUsed: 本草綱目 Bencao Gangmu, 卷18上 (1596)
神農本草經 Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan recension (1799)
本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin, 吳儀洛, 卷五草部 (1757)

clinical_contraindications.text: 夏月少使人參發心痃之病
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 斆曰 Lei Xiao (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上 正誤, 1596)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: In the summer months use ginseng sparingly; it provokes the disorder of 心痃 (a heart/epigastric knotted-pain condition).

clinical_contraindications.text: 凡酒色過度損傷肺腎真隂隂虚火動勞{{SKchar|1033}}吐血欬血等證勿用之
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 王綸曰 Wang Lun (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上 正誤, 1596)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: In all cases of excess in wine and sex damaging the true yin of lung and kidney, yin deficiency with stirring fire, taxation cough(?), blood vomiting, blood-streaked cough and the like, do not use it. VERBATIM CAUTION: the Siku transcription leaves one glyph unrendered as {{SKchar|1033}} exactly where a reading of 嗽 (cough, giving 勞嗽) has been proposed; 嗽 is the submitter's reading, NOT visible text in this recension, so the placeholder is preserved here rather than silently resolved.

clinical_contraindications.text: 葢人參入手太隂能補火故肺受火邪者忌之
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 王綸曰 Wang Lun (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上 正誤, 1596)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Because ginseng enters the hand-taiyin (lung) and can supplement fire, those whose lungs have received fire-evil must avoid it. Rationale clause continuous with the prohibition above.

clinical_contraindications.text: 若誤用參耆甘温之劑則病日増服之過多則死不可治
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 王綸曰 Wang Lun (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上 正誤, 1596)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: If sweet-warm formulas of ginseng and astragalus are used in error the illness worsens daily; taken in excess it kills and cannot be treated. Severity clause of the same prohibition.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug, and 參耆 (ginseng + astragalus) sweet-warm formulas

clinical_contraindications.text: 但闭氣。肺有火熱。及肺氣不利者忌之。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新, 1757)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: It does however block qi. Those with fire-heat in the lung, and those whose lung qi is not free-flowing, must avoid it. (Wikisource transcription uses simplified 闭.)

clinical_contraindications.text: 實表。表有邪者忌之。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新, 1757)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: It solidifies the exterior. Those with evil lodged in the exterior must avoid it.

clinical_contraindications.text: 凡痧痘斑毒。欲出未出。但闷熱而不見點。若誤用之。以阻截其路。爲祸尤烈。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新, 1757)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: In all cases of measles/pox/rash-toxin about to erupt but not yet erupted, where there is only stifling heat and no spots visible, using it in error blocks off their route of exit and the harm is especially fierce. (Transcription's simplified 闷/祸 preserved.)

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 Xu Zhicai (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上, 1596)
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Is antagonised by Sou Shu (Deutzia) and Lu Xian (mineral salt/bittern).

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 Xu Zhicai (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上, 1596)
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: OPPOSES Li Lu (Veratrum). One of the 十八反 Eighteen Antagonisms.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 Xu Zhicai / 一云 alternate tradition (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上, 1596)
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: One tradition says: fears / is diminished by Wu Ling Zhi (flying-squirrel faeces). The 一云 marks this as a variant reading, not the main line.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 Xu Zhicai / 一云 alternate tradition (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上, 1596)
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Is antagonised by Zao Jia (gleditsia pod) and black soybean. Part of the same 一云 variant run.

drug_incompatibilities.text: 震亨曰人參入手大隂與藜蘆相反服參一兩入藜蘆一錢其功盡廢也
drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 震亨曰 Zhu Zhenheng (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上, 1596)
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Ginseng enters the hand-taiyin and is MUTUALLY OPPOSED (相反) to Li Lu: take one liang of ginseng with one qian of Li Lu and its efficacy is entirely destroyed. Note this is one continuous sentence in the source; the channel-entry statement and the antagonism statement are not separate lines.

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 Xu Zhicai (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12上, 1596)
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Fu Ling (Poria) and Ma Lin (Iris lactea) act as its ENVOYS, guiding partners that direct it in a formula.

unclassified: 動紫石英 (之才曰, 本草綱目 卷12上, 1596) — 'stirs / agitates Zi Shi Ying (fluorite)'. 動 is NOT one of the three negative seven-relations terms (畏惡反), so it cannot be filed as an incompatibility under the permitted relation values; nor is it a benefit the herb confers, so it is not a positive pairing. It closes the 一云 variant run 「一云畏五靈脂惡皂莢黑豆動紫石英」 and is preserved here rather than being forced into a bucket.
sourcesUsed: 本草綱目 Bencao Gangmu, 四庫全書本, 卷十二上 (1596)
本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin, 吳儀洛 (1757)

clinical_contraindications.text: 但不得用野菊名苦薏者爾
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍 Li Shizhen (本草綱目 卷十五 氣味 note, 1596)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Only, one must not use the wild chrysanthemum, the one called Ku Yi. A prohibition on the material itself rather than on a patient state.
clinical_contraindications.scope: identity/adulterant: prohibits 野菊 (wild chrysanthemum, 苦薏), NOT the true 甘菊 that is the drug

clinical_contraindications.text: 故景煥牧竪閑談云真菊延齡野菊泄人正如黄精益夀鉤吻殺人之意
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 景煥 Jing Huan, 牧竪閑談, quoted by 時珍 (本草綱目 卷十五, 1596)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Hence Jing Huan's Mu Shu Xian Tan says: true chrysanthemum extends the years, wild chrysanthemum purges (drains) a person, exactly in the sense that Huang Jing benefits longevity while Gou Wen kills. States the harm from the wrong species.
clinical_contraindications.scope: identity/adulterant: harm attaches to 野菊, not to the true drug

clinical_contraindications.text: （花小味苦者、名苦薏、非真菊也、景焕牧竖闲談云：真菊延龄、野菊瀉人。）
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新 卷三草部, 1757, 甘菊花)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Those with small flowers and a bitter taste are called Ku Yi and are not the true chrysanthemum; Jing Huan's Mu Shu Xian Tan says true chrysanthemum extends the years, wild chrysanthemum purges a person. Wu Yiluo repeats the same adulterant prohibition. Orthography note: this Wikisource transcription uses simplified 焕/竖/谈/龄/瀉 where the BCGM line reads 煥/竪/談/齡/泄.
clinical_contraindications.scope: identity/adulterant: 苦薏 / 野菊, not the true drug

unclassified: 一種青莖而大作蒿艾氣味苦不堪食者名苦薏非真菊也葉正相似惟以甘苦别之 (陶弘景 Tao Hongjing, 集解, 本草綱目 卷十五, 1596) — botanical DIFFERENTIATION note: one kind with green stems, large, giving off an artemisia smell, bitter in taste and unfit to eat, is called Ku Yi and is not the true chrysanthemum; the leaves look just alike, and only sweet-versus-bitter tells them apart. 不堪食 describes the adulterant's unfitness, not a dietary avoidance for the drug, and the clause states no prohibition of its own, so it is a descriptive identification aid rather than a warning.

家园所種。杭產者良。 … 有黃白二種。单瓣味甘者入藥。 (吳儀洛, 本草從新 1757) — SOURCING and SELECTION guidance: garden-grown, Hangzhou produce is best; there are yellow and white kinds; the single-petalled sweet-tasting sort is the one that enters medicine. A quality specification, not a contraindication. Recorded so the bracketed adulterant warning is seen to have been lifted out of an otherwise non-prohibitive sentence rather than the whole line being filed as a warning.

本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin, 卷三草部 (1757)

items.herb: Goji / Gou Qi Zi 枸杞子

clinical_contraindications.text: 便滑者勿用。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新 卷九木部 灌木類, 1757, 枸杞子)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Those with slippery stools (loose bowels) must not use it.

clinical_contraindications.text: 有痼疾人勿服
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草綱目 卷36 附方 (1596)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: People with a chronic/entrenched illness must not take it. SCOPE WARNING: this clause attaches to a 附方 (appended formula) built on 枸杞根 (the ROOT, i.e. Di Gu Pi), NOT to the berry. It must not be promoted into a herb-level contraindication for goji berries.
clinical_contraindications.scope: a single 附方 (appended formula) using 枸杞根 (root) — formula-level and root-level only, NOT the berry

unclassified: 至于子則甘平而潤性滋而補不能退熱止能補腎潤肺生精益氣此乃平補之藥 (本草綱目 卷36 發明, 1596) — PROPERTIES statement about the berry: sweet, neutral and moistening, enriching and supplementing in nature; it CANNOT reduce heat, it can only supplement the kidney, moisten the lung, generate essence and boost qi; it is a balanced tonic. 不能退熱 is a limit on what the drug does, not a prohibition on who may take it, so it is neither a contraindication nor a pairing. Filed here so the limitation is not lost.

南方樹止數尺。北方並是大樹。以甘州所產。紅潤少核者佳。酒潤搗。 (吳儀洛, 本草從新 1757) — SOURCING and PROCESSING note immediately following 便滑者勿用: southern plants are only a few feet tall, northern ones are large trees; Ganzhou produce, red and plump with few seeds, is best; moisten with wine and pound. Not a warning. Recorded so the prohibition is seen to have been cut cleanly from the sentence run that follows it.
VERIFIED ABSENCE: the whole BCGM 枸杞 entry was read for any other prohibition attaching to the BERRY and none was found. The only near-neighbour is 有痼疾人勿服, which is filed above with its 枸杞根 附方 scope.

items.herb: Capillaris Wormwood / Yin Chen Hao 茵陳蒿

clinical_contraindications.text: 按黃胆須分陰黃、陽黃。陽黃宜茵陳。陰黃宜溫補。若用茵陳。多致不救。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (按, i.e. the author's own note; 本草從新, 1757, 茵陳)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Note: in jaundice one must distinguish yin jaundice from yang jaundice. Yang jaundice is suited to Yin Chen. Yin jaundice calls for warming and supplementing; if Yin Chen is used there it most often leads to a case beyond saving. The prohibition is the 陰黃 half: Yin Chen is contraindicated in yin-type jaundice. Kept as one verbatim block because the yang-jaundice clause is what defines the boundary of the prohibition. Orthography note: 胆 for 疸 is the Wikisource transcription's, not an introduced error.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug (茵陳), restricted to the 陰黃 (yin jaundice) presentation

sourcesUsed: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin, 吳儀洛 (1757)

items.herb: Chinese Senega / Polygala (Yuan Zhi) 遠志

clinical_contraindications.text: 不可多用獨用。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新, 1757)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: It must not be used in large amounts nor used alone.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug — dosage and solo-use restriction

clinical_contraindications.text: 純虚無滞者忌。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新, 1757)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Those of pure deficiency with no stagnation must avoid it. 忌 here is followed by a PATIENT STATE, so this is clinical, not dietary.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 Xu Zhicai (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12下 氣味 note, 1596)
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Fears / is diminished by Zhen Zhu (pearl), Li Lu (Veratrum), Fei Lian (cockroach) and Qi Ge. Note the BCGM immediately follows this with a dispute over what 齊蛤 even is (see unclassified), and the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension omits 齊蛤 from the list altogether.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新, 1757)
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Fears / is diminished by pearl and Veratrum. Wu Yiluo carries only two of the four.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 神農本草經 七情 appendix, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), juan 3
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Fears / is diminished by pearl, cockroach and Veratrum. Three of the four; 齊蛤 absent from this recension.

positive_pairings.text: 逺志小草得茯苓冬葵子龍骨良
positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 Xu Zhicai (quoted in 本草綱目 卷12下 氣味 note, 1596)
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Yuan Zhi AND Xiao Cao (the aerial part) are improved by obtaining Fu Ling (Poria), Dong Kui Zi (mallow seed) and Long Gu (dragon bone) — a beneficial combination, filed as 'other' because 得…良 is a benefit-from-combination formula rather than a named 使/相須 term. SCOPE: the clause names 小草 alongside 遠志, so the relation set covers the aerial part as well as the root.

positive_pairings.speaker: 吳儀洛 (本草從新, 1757)
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Improved by obtaining Poria and dragon bone. Wu Yiluo drops 冬葵子 from the triad.

positive_pairings.speaker: 神農本草經 七情 appendix, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), juan 3
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Improved by obtaining Poria, mallow seed and dragon bone. Full triad, matching Xu Zhicai.

positive_pairings.speaker: 神農本草經 七情 appendix, Sun Xingyan recension (1799), juan 3
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE, AND CRITICAL NOT TO INVERT. Yuan Zhi NEUTRALISES the toxicity of Tian Xiong and Fu Zi (aconite preparations) — i.e. it makes aconite safer. This is an antidote capability of the herb. Filed as an incompatibility it would read 'do not combine with aconite', the exact opposite of what the source says.

unclassified: 𢎞景曰藥無齊蛤恐是百合也 (陶弘景 Tao Hongjing, quoted in 本草綱目 卷12下, 1596) — IDENTITY DISPUTE, not a pairing: 'among the drugs there is no Qi Ge; it is probably Bai He (lily).' Bears on which drug the 畏齊蛤 clause actually names.
權曰是蠐螬也 (權曰 Zhen Quan, quoted in 本草綱目 卷12下, 1596) — IDENTITY DISPUTE: 'it is Qi Cao (grub).' Second competing identification of 齊蛤.

恭曰藥録下卷有齊蛤陶說非也 (恭曰 Su Gong, quoted in 本草綱目 卷12下, 1596) — IDENTITY DISPUTE: 'the lower juan of the Yao Lu does contain Qi Ge; Tao's account is wrong.' Third position. All three are recorded because the 畏齊蛤 entry above is only as reliable as the identification of 齊蛤, which the BCGM itself leaves unsettled.

clinical_contraindications.text: 月事過多。强陽不痿。小便不利者。不宜用。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷九木部 — unattributed in the text itself
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Not suitable for use in THREE states: (1) 月事過多 excessive menstruation; (2) 强陽不痿 persistent strong yang that will not subside (priapism); (3) 小便不利 inhibited urination. All three are governed by the single closing verb 不宜用.

clinical_contraindications.text: 去核。（核能滑精。）
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷九木部
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Remove the pit. The pit can cause seminal leakage (滑精). A part-level caution and processing instruction, not a whole-drug prohibition.
clinical_contraindications.scope: a named part — the pit/stone (核) only

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), quoted in 本草綱目 卷36 氣味 note, 1596
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by Platycodon (桔梗), Saposhnikovia (防風) and Stephania (防己).

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 神農本草經 孫星衍輯本 (1799), 卷三 七情 appendix, s.v. 山茱萸
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Independent corroboration of the same three antagonists in the Sun Xingyan recension.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷九木部, closing line
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Same three antagonists, in Wu Yiluo's reordering (防己 first).

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), quoted in 本草綱目 卷36 氣味 note, 1596
positive_pairings.gloss: Polygonum fruit (蓼實) acts as its ENVOY / guiding partner. POSITIVE — a pairing instruction, not a warning.

positive_pairings.speaker: 神農本草經 孫星衍輯本 (1799), 卷三 七情 appendix, s.v. 山茱萸
positive_pairings.gloss: Same envoy relation in the Sun Xingyan recension. POSITIVE.

unclassified: 「陳久者良。」 (本草從新 1757, 卷九木部) — a quality/ageing note: long-aged material is better. Neither a prohibition, a diet note, nor a drug relation; carried here so it is not lost.

clinical_contraindications.text: 下部無風寒溼邪而有火。及肝腎虚而有火者。勿服。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷九木部, immediately after 酿酒尤良（王纶曰…）
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Do not take it where the lower body has no wind-cold-damp evil but does have fire, nor where liver and kidney are deficient with fire present.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), quoted in 本草綱目 卷36 五加, 根皮 氣味 note, 1596
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by Scrophularia (玄參) and snake slough (蛇皮).

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 神農本草經 孫星衍輯本 (1799) 七情 appendix, s.v. 五加皮
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Variant reading of the SAME relation with a different verb: the Sun Xingyan recension has 畏 (fears / is diminished by) where BCGM has 惡. Recorded separately because the verb differs by source; the drugs are the same two.

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), quoted in 本草綱目 卷36 五加, 根皮 氣味 note, 1596
positive_pairings.gloss: Polygala (遠志) acts as its ENVOY / guiding partner. POSITIVE — a pairing instruction, not a warning.

clinical_contraindications.text: 然食多則收令太過令人氣壅臚脹昏頓故物類相感志言銀杏能醉人而三元延壽書言白果食滿千箇者死又云昔有飢者同以白果代飯食飽次日皆死也
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草綱目 卷30 發明 (1596) — unattributed within the quoted run; the passage itself cites 物類相感志 and 三元延壽書
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Eating much of it makes the astringing action excessive, causing qi congestion, abdominal distension and stupor. Cited reports: the 物類相感志 says ginkgo can intoxicate; the 三元延壽書 says one who eats a full thousand nuts dies, and records starving people who ate them in place of rice and were all dead the next day. An overdose / lethality warning.

clinical_contraindications.text: 時珍曰熟食小苦微甘性温有小毒多食令人臚脹
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), 本草綱目 卷30 氣味 note, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Cooked it is slightly bitter, faintly sweet, warm in nature, and SLIGHTLY TOXIC (有小毒); eating much of it causes abdominal distension.

clinical_contraindications.text: 瑞曰多食壅氣動風小兒多食昏霍發驚引疳
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 瑞曰 (Wu Rui, 吳瑞), 本草綱目 卷30 氣味 note, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Eating much congests qi and stirs wind; in children, eating much causes clouding and sudden derangement, provokes fright convulsions and brings on gan (malnutrition) disorder. Note: the eel clause that follows in the same run is filed under dietary avoidances.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; the second half is specific to children (小兒)

clinical_contraindications.text: 多食則收濇太過。令人壅氣胪胀。小兒發驚动疳。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷十
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Eating much makes the astringing-binding action excessive, congesting qi and distending the abdomen; in children it provokes fright and stirs gan disorder.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; final clause specific to children

dietary_avoidances.speaker: 瑞曰 (Wu Rui, 吳瑞), 本草綱目 卷30 氣味 note, 1596
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Eaten together with eel (鰻鱺魚) it brings on 軟風 (soft wind). A food-combining avoidance, not a drug incompatibility and not a clinical prohibition.

clinical_contraindications.text: 宗奭曰柴胡本經並無一字治勞今人治勞方中鮮有不用者嗚呼凡此誤世甚多…若此等病茍無實熱醫者執而用之不死何待
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 宗奭曰 (Kou Zongshi), 本草綱目 卷13 發明, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: The Bencao Jing says not one word about Chai Hu treating taxation (勞); today it is in nearly every taxation formula, and this has misled the age greatly. In such diseases, if there is no genuine repletion heat and the physician insists on using it, what can follow but death. A prohibition on use in taxation without repletion heat.

clinical_contraindications.text: 時珍曰…惟勞在肺腎者不用可爾
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), 本草綱目 卷13 發明, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Only where the taxation is seated in lung and kidney should it not be used.

clinical_contraindications.text: 陰虚火炎氣升者。禁用。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 柴胡 entry
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Forbidden where yin is deficient with flaring fire and ascending qi.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), 本草綱目 卷13, 1596
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by Gleditsia pod (皂莢).

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), 本草綱目 卷13, 1596
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Fears / is diminished by Aster fastigiatus (女菀) and Veratrum (藜蘆).

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), 本草綱目 卷13, 1596
positive_pairings.gloss: Pinellia (半夏) acts as its ENVOY / guiding partner. POSITIVE — a pairing instruction, not a warning.

clinical_contraindications.text: 然必少壯氣盛能食者用之相宜若中氣不足而邪火熾甚者久服則有寒中之變近時虚損及縱慾求嗣之人用補陰藥往往以此二味為君日日服餌降令太過脾胃受傷真陽暗損精氣不暖致生他病蓋不知此物苦寒而滑滲且苦味久服有反從火化之害故葉氏醫學統㫖有四物加知母黄蘗久服傷胃不能生陰之戒
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), 本草綱目 卷三十五上 發明, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Suitable only for the young, strong, qi-abundant and good-eating. Where centre qi is insufficient while evil fire blazes, long use brings cold-in-the-centre transformation. People with deficiency-detriment, and those indulging desire while seeking heirs, commonly make this pair (知母 + 黄蘗) sovereign in yin-supplementing medicine and take it daily; the downbearing is excessive, spleen and stomach are damaged, true yang is covertly drained, essence-qi is not warmed, and other diseases arise. They do not know the drug is bitter-cold, slippery and percolating, and that a bitter flavour long taken carries the harm of paradoxically transforming into fire. Hence Ye's 醫學統㫖 warns that Si Wu Tang plus 知母 and 黄蘗, long taken, damages the stomach and cannot engender yin.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; the central warning is specifically about the 知母＋黄蘗 pair used as sovereign in yin-supplementing formulas, incl. 四物加知母黄蘗

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), 本草綱目 卷三十五上 氣味 note (not 發明), 1596
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by dried lacquer (乾漆).

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), 本草綱目 卷三十五上 氣味 note, 1596
positive_pairings.gloss: It SUBDUES / controls sulphur (硫黄). POSITIVE — a capability of the drug acting on another substance, NOT a prohibition against combining with sulphur. Quoted contiguously with 惡乾漆 in the source (「之才曰惡乾漆伏硫黄」) but the two verbs point in opposite directions.

unclassified: NO CLASSICAL MATERIAL EXISTS for this drug. The verified record states that no 雲芝 entry appears anywhere in the complete 52-juan 本草綱目 (1596) or in 神農本草經 (孫星衍輯本, 1799); therefore no contraindication of any kind can be sourced for Trametes versicolor. All four buckets are correctly empty.

DELIBERATE NON-CARRY (recorded so the omission is auditable, not accidental): the neighbouring 芝 entry contains Xu Zhicai's 惡常山 and 畏扁青、茵蔯蒿. That material belongs to Ganoderma (靈芝), NOT to 雲芝/Trametes versicolor, and the verified record explicitly instructs that it must not be carried across. It is therefore intentionally excluded from this herb's incompatibilities.

clinical_contraindications.text: 中寒下陷者忌之。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 百合 entry, closing clause
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Avoid it where there is cold in the centre with downward sinking (中寒下陷). 忌 here governs a PATIENT STATE, not a food, so this is a clinical prohibition rather than a dietary note. Rationale supported by the entry's earlier 「利二便」 / 「善通二便」 — it moves the two excretions, which would worsen sinking.

unclassified: 「善通二便。」 (本草從新 1757) — an INDICATION / action statement (it freely opens the two excretions), quoted in the record as the rationale for the contraindication that follows. Not itself a prohibition, so it is not filed as one; kept here so no part of the closing run is dropped.

「花白者入藥。」 (本草從新 1757) — a selection/identification note: the white-flowered kind is the one used medicinally. Neither a warning nor a pairing; recorded so the verbatim closing run 「善通二便。中寒下陷者忌之。花白者入藥。」 is fully accounted for.
sourcesUsed: 本草從新 Ben Cao Cong Xin, 吳儀洛 (1757)

clinical_contraindications.text: 一切客寒犯胃。溼氣侵脾之證。但可施於元氣未虚。邪氣方盛。若脾胃虚者。切勿沾唇。虽一時未見其害。而清純冲和之氣。潜傷默耗矣。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷八木部 厚朴
clinical_contraindications.gloss: For all patterns of guest-cold assailing the stomach and damp qi invading the spleen it may be applied ONLY where original qi is not yet deficient and evil qi is at its height. Where spleen and stomach are deficient, on no account let it touch the lips: though no harm is seen at the time, the clear, pure, harmonious qi is covertly damaged and silently consumed.

clinical_contraindications.text: 孕妇服之。大損胎元。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷八木部 厚朴
clinical_contraindications.gloss: If a pregnant woman takes it, it greatly damages the foetal origin. Pregnancy contraindication.

clinical_contraindications.text: 元素曰…孕婦忌之三也…誤服脫人元氣
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 元素曰 (Zhang Yuansu), 本草綱目 卷35上 發明, 1596
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Third of Zhang Yuansu's cautions: pregnant women must avoid it; taken in error it strips a person's original qi. 忌 here governs a PATIENT STATE (pregnancy), so clinical, not dietary. This is a second, independent pregnancy warning distinct from the 本草從新 one above.

dietary_avoidances.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷八木部 厚朴
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Avoid beans (豆); transgressing this stirs the qi. A food-combining avoidance, not a clinical prohibition and not a drug incompatibility.
dietary_avoidances.scope: whole drug, as diet during use

dietary_avoidances.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai) as the line stands in 本草綱目 卷35上 氣味 note, 1596
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Avoid beans; eating them stirs the qi. Provenance nuance recorded in the source material: BCGM runs this clause on to Xu Zhicai's seven-relations line, but 證類本草 (1108) attributes it instead to 藥性論 (see next entry). Substance identical either way.
dietary_avoidances.scope: whole drug, as diet during use

dietary_avoidances.text: 藥性論云厚朴臣忌豆食之者動氣
dietary_avoidances.speaker: 藥性論 (Yaoxing Lun), quoted in 證類本草 卷13, 1108
dietary_avoidances.gloss: The Yaoxing Lun's own wording: Hou Po is a minister drug; avoid beans, for one who eats them has the qi stirred. Kept verbatim as the earliest attribution of the bean avoidance.
dietary_avoidances.scope: whole drug, as diet during use

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷八木部 厚朴
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by Alisma (澤瀉) and niter (硝石). Two drugs only in this recension.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), 本草綱目 卷35上 氣味 note, 1596
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by Alisma (澤瀉), niter (硝石) and glauberite/gypsum-type mineral 寒水石. NOTE the third item: BCGM carries 寒水石, which 本草從新 omits.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 證類本草 卷13, 1108
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Same three antagonists in the Zhenglei recension, with 消石 written for 硝石. Confirms 寒水石 belongs in the list.

positive_pairings.speaker: 本草從新 (吳儀洛, 1757), 卷八木部 厚朴
positive_pairings.gloss: Dried ginger (乾薑) acts as its ENVOY / guiding partner. POSITIVE — a pairing instruction, not a warning.

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), 本草綱目 卷35上 氣味 note (1596); identically in 證類本草 卷13 (1108)
positive_pairings.gloss: Same envoy relation, attested in both BCGM and the earlier Zhenglei Bencao. POSITIVE.

clinical_contraindications.text: 若血虚痉急。頭痛不因風寒。（内傷。）泄瀉不因寒溼。火升作嗽。陰虚盗汗。陽虚自汗者。竝禁用。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (Wu Yiluo), 本草從新 1757, unattributed compiler voice
clinical_contraindications.gloss: All prohibited: blood-deficiency spasm/tetany; headache NOT caused by wind-cold (i.e. internal damage); diarrhoea NOT caused by cold-damp; cough from fire rising; yin-deficiency night sweats; yang-deficiency spontaneous sweating.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), BCGM 卷13 氣味 note
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Fears / is diminished by bi xie (Dioscorea hypoglauca).

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), BCGM 卷13 氣味 note
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by li lu (Veratrum), bai lian, dried ginger, yuan hua.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan 1799 recension, 七情 appendix 卷三
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by dried ginger, li lu, bai lian, yuan hua. Same four-item list as BCGM, different order and punctuation.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 吳儀洛 (Wu Yiluo), 本草從新 1757, 防風
drug_incompatibilities.gloss: Antagonised by dried ginger, bai lian, yuan hua. This 1757 list omits li lu.

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), BCGM 卷13 氣味 note
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Fang Feng NEUTRALISES the toxicity of fu zi (aconite). It makes aconite safer. This is NOT a prohibition on combining the two.

positive_pairings.speaker: Shennong Bencao Jing, Sun Xingyan 1799 recension, 七情 appendix 卷三
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Neutralises aconite toxicity. Independent corroboration of the same claim.

positive_pairings.speaker: 吳儀洛 (Wu Yiluo), 本草從新 1757, 防風
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Neutralises aconite toxicity. Third independent witness.

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), BCGM 卷13 氣味 note
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Combined with cong bai (scallion white) it can travel through the whole body.

positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), BCGM 卷13 氣味 note
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Combined with ze xie and gao ben it treats wind.

positive_pairings.text: 得當歸芍藥陽起石禹餘粮療婦人子臓風
positive_pairings.speaker: 之才曰 (Xu Zhicai), BCGM 卷13 氣味 note
positive_pairings.gloss: POSITIVE. Combined with dang gui, shao yao, yang qi shi and yu yu liang it treats wind in the womb in women.

clinical_contraindications.text: 苦寒久食令人痩去人脂使人不睡
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 藏器曰 (Chen Cangqi 陳藏器), BCGM 卷32 茗 葉氣味 note
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Bitter and cold; long consumption makes a person thin, strips body fat, and prevents sleep.

clinical_contraindications.text: 飲之宜熱冷則聚痰
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 藏器曰 (Chen Cangqi 陳藏器), BCGM 卷32 茗 葉氣味 note
clinical_contraindications.gloss: It should be drunk hot; drunk cold it gathers phlegm.

clinical_contraindications.text: 大渴及酒後飲茶水入腎經令人腰脚膀胱冷痛兼患水腫攣痺諸疾
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 李廷飛曰 (Li Tingfei), BCGM 卷32 茗 葉氣味 note
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Drinking tea in great thirst or after wine sends the water into the kidney channel, causing cold pain in the lower back, legs and bladder, plus oedema, cramping and numbness disorders.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug (leaf); patient states of extreme thirst and post-alcohol

clinical_contraindications.text: 大抵飲茶宜熱宜少不飲尤佳空腹最忌
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 李廷飛曰 (Li Tingfei), BCGM 卷32 茗 葉氣味 note
clinical_contraindications.gloss: In general tea should be drunk hot and in small amount; not drinking it is better still; on an empty stomach is the most forbidden. NOTE: the source-verification remark flags this sixth caution as previously un-harvested.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug (leaf); 空腹 empty stomach

clinical_contraindications.text: 若虚寒及血弱之人飲之既久則脾胃惡寒元氣暗損土不制水精血潛虚成痰飲成痞脹成痿痺成黄痩成嘔逆成洞瀉成腹痛成疝瘕種種内傷此茶之害也
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), BCGM 卷32 茗 發明
clinical_contraindications.gloss: In people of deficiency-cold or weak blood, long drinking makes spleen and stomach averse to cold, secretly damages original qi, earth fails to control water, essence and blood covertly empty; producing phlegm-rheum, glomus distension, atrophy-numbness, yellow emaciation, retching, throughflux diarrhoea, abdominal pain, hernia-conglomeration — every kind of internal damage. This is the harm of tea.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug (leaf); patients of 虚寒 or 血弱

clinical_contraindications.text: 服威靈仙土茯苓者忌飲茶
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), BCGM 卷32 茗 葉氣味 note
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Those taking wei ling xian or tu fu ling must avoid drinking tea. Filed as clinical because it prohibits the herb given a patient's concurrent medication; it is NOT one of the three 七情 negative relations (畏/惡/反), so it cannot go in drug_incompatibilities.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug (leaf); patients concurrently taking 威靈仙 or 土茯苓

dietary_avoidances.speaker: 胡洽曰 (Hu Qia), BCGM 卷32 茗 葉氣味 note
dietary_avoidances.gloss: Eaten together with fei (torreya nut) it makes the body heavy. Food-combining lore, not a clinical prohibition.

unclassified: 「時珍早年盛氣毎飲新茗必至數椀輕汗發而肌骨清頗覺痛快中年胃氣稍損飲之即覺為害不痞悶嘔惡即腹冷洞泄故備述諸說以警同好焉」 (時珍曰, BCGM 卷32 發明) — Li Shizhen's first-person autobiographical account: in youth, vigorous qi, several bowls of new tea gave light sweat and clear flesh and bone; in middle age with stomach qi somewhat damaged, drinking it immediately harmed him, either glomus-oppression and retching or cold abdomen and throughflux diarrhoea; hence he sets out all these opinions to warn fellow enthusiasts. Testimony/narrative that motivates the warnings rather than stating a rule; not filed as a prohibition in its own right.
sourcesUsed: 本草綱目 Bencao Gangmu, 1596, juan 32 (果部)

clinical_contraindications.text: 辛熱純陽走氣助火昬目發瘡
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), BCGM 卷32 氣味
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Acrid, hot, pure yang; it races the qi and aids fire, dims the eyes and raises sores.

clinical_contraindications.text: 多食損肺令人吐血
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 珣曰 (Li Xun 李珣), BCGM 卷32 氣味
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Eaten in quantity it damages the lung and causes a person to vomit blood.

clinical_contraindications.text: 胡椒屬火而性燥食之快膈喜之者衆積久則脾胃肺氣大傷凡病氣疾人益大其禍也
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 震亨曰 (Zhu Zhenheng), BCGM 卷32 發明
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Pepper belongs to fire and is drying; eating it eases the diaphragm so many are fond of it, but accumulated over time it greatly damages spleen, stomach and lung qi; in anyone suffering a qi disorder it magnifies the calamity.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; prolonged use, and patients with qi disorders

clinical_contraindications.text: 胡椒大辛熱純陽之物腸胃寒濕者宜之熱病人食之䡃火傷氣隂受其害
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), BCGM 卷32 發明
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Pepper is greatly acrid, hot, a pure-yang substance; suitable for those with cold-damp in intestines and stomach, but if a person with a heat disease eats it, it stirs fire, damages qi, and the yin suffers harm. Clause carries an indication (cold-damp) and its mirrored contraindication (heat disease) in one run; kept whole.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug; patients with heat disease

clinical_contraindications.text: 病咽㗋口齒者亦宜忌之
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍曰 (Li Shizhen), BCGM 卷32 發明
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Those with throat, mouth or tooth disease should likewise avoid it.

clinical_contraindications.text: 然損肺走氣。动火动血。損齒昏目。發瘡痔臟毒。必陰氣至足者。方可用。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (Wu Yiluo), 本草從新 卷十, 1757
clinical_contraindications.gloss: However it damages the lung and races the qi, stirs fire and stirs blood, damages the teeth and dims the eyes, raises sores, haemorrhoids and visceral toxin. Only one whose yin qi is fully sufficient may use it. (Transcription uses simplified 动 for 動.)

unclassified: 「時珍自少嗜之嵗嵗病目而不疑及也後漸知其[未鐫之字]遂痛絶之目病亦止纔食一二粒即便昏澀此乃昔人所未試者」 (時珍曰, BCGM 卷32 發明) — Li Shizhen's autobiographical testimony: fond of pepper from youth, suffered eye disease year after year without suspecting it; on realising, he cut it off entirely and the eye disease stopped; even one or two grains now brings blurring and grittiness — something earlier writers never tested. Narrative evidence rather than a stated rule, so not filed as a prohibition. clinical_contraindications.gloss: Whenever the disease is in the qi division, or there is stomach cold, or blood deficiency, and in pregnancy and after childbirth — in all these do not use it lightly, because its nature is bitter-cold and can damage original qi and consume yin blood. The pregnancy caution is 1596 text, not a modern interpolation.

clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 (Wu Yiluo), 本草從新 1757, 卷一草部 山草類 知母
clinical_contraindications.gloss: It damages the stomach and makes the intestines slippery; it causes a person to purge.

drug_incompatibilities.speaker: 吳儀洛 (Wu Yiluo), 本草從新 當歸, 1757

clinical_contraindications.speaker: 震亨曰 (Zhu Zhenheng)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Huang Qi supplements original qi and suits those who are pale, plump and sweat a lot; but if the face is dark and the body solid and thin, taking it causes chest fullness, and San-ao Tang should be used to drain it.

clinical_contraindications.text: 咽乾乃虚中有熱不可服涼藥…
clinical_contraindications.speaker: unattributed 附方 note (BCGM 欬膿血 formula)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Dry throat means heat within deficiency; cooling drugs must not be taken.

VERIFIED ABSENCE, not a clause: Dutt 1877 pp.105-107 (Guduchi; Beng. Gulancha) is entirely indications and formulae (Dhatrimodaka, Guduchyadi taila, Vrihat/Vata guduchyadi taila) with no caution, restriction or incompatibility; Dymock 1890 likewise gives only uses in fever, rheumatism and jaundice. The absence holds across these two reachable pre-1900 works only — Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya and the Sanskrit originals were not consulted.

clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo (本草從新 1757, 砂仁)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Acrid, penetrating and drying in nature; those with blood deficiency and flaring fire must not use it.

clinical_contraindications.text: 胎妇多服耗氣。必致難產。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo (本草從新 1757, 砂仁)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: If a pregnant woman takes much of it, it consumes qi and will certainly cause difficult labour. Note: this is a DOSE limit in pregnancy (多服), not a blanket pregnancy ban — the same drug is used to calm the fetus in BCGM (see unclassified).

unclassified: 「出岭南。炒去衣研。」 (本草從新 1757) — provenance (Lingnan) and processing instruction (dry-fry, remove the husk, grind). Not a warning.

「和中行氣止痛安胎{{SK notes|楊士瀛}}」 (BCGM 1596 卷十四 主治, attributed 楊士瀛 Yang Shiying) — 主治/indications context: harmonises the centre, moves qi, stops pain, CALMS THE FETUS. Direction is treats-not-causes; it is the countervailing evidence to the pregnancy dose limit above, not itself a caution.

positive_pairings.gloss: Fang Feng (Saposhnikovia) and Di Yu (Sanguisorba) act as its envoys/guides.

positive_pairings.gloss: For both Atractylodes (bai zhu and cang zhu), Fang Feng and Di Yu are the envoys. This confirms the envoy pair applies to Cang Zhu too.

unclassified: 「入足太隂陽明手太隂陽明太陽之經　忌同白术」 (BCGM 1596 卷十二下, end of the 蒼术氣味 note) — AMBIGUOUS AND FLAGGED. Held here rather than filed under either bucket so a reviewer decides. The channel-entry clause preceding it (足太陰/陽明, 手太陰/陽明/太陽) is meridian attribution, not a warning.

clinical_contraindications.text: …若因飲寒受寒腹中痛及飲水心下悸小便不利而脉不數者是裏無熱證則黄芩不可用也若熱厥腹痛肺熱而小便不利者黄芩其可不用乎
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 時珍 (Li Shizhen), BCGM 卷十三 發明
clinical_contraindications.gloss: If abdominal pain comes from drinking cold or contracting cold, or there is palpitation below the heart from drinking water with inhibited urination and a non-rapid pulse, this is an interior WITHOUT heat, and Huang Qin may not be used. But for heat-reversal abdominal pain, or lung heat with inhibited urination, how could Huang Qin not be used?

clinical_contraindications.text: 震亨曰黄芩降痰假其降火也…若肺虛者多用則傷肺必先以天門冬保定肺氣而後用之
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 震亨曰 (Zhu Zhenheng), BCGM 卷十三 發明
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Huang Qin brings phlegm down by way of bringing fire down; but in lung deficiency, using much of it injures the lung — one must first secure lung qi with Tian Men Dong (Asparagus) and only then use it. A qualified caution, not an absolute ban: the proviso names the corrective partner.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug, lung-deficiency patients, high dose

clinical_contraindications.text: 苦寒傷胃。虚寒者。均宜戒。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo (本草從新 1757, 黃芩)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Bitter and cold, it injures the stomach; those with deficiency-cold should all abstain from it.

clinical_contraindications.text: 胎前若非實熱而服之。陰損胎元矣。
clinical_contraindications.speaker: 吳儀洛 Wu Yiluo (本草從新 1757, 黃芩)
clinical_contraindications.gloss: Taken before birth when the pattern is NOT excess heat, it covertly damages the fetal origin. A qualified pregnancy caution: BCGM records the calm-the-fetus use only under heat patterns.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug, pregnancy, absent an excess-heat pattern

clinical_contraindications.gloss: In a deficient person, even where there is glomus and accumulation, one must first nourish stomach qi; once the stomach is strong the hard accumulation is gradually ground down and dispersed. This [drug] is not suitable to use — its foul pungency further injures stomach qi.
clinical_contraindications.scope: whole drug. Patient-state prohibition (虚人 / deficient constitution), preceded in the same passage by the rationale 「人之血氣。闻香則順。闻臭則逆。」 (a person's blood and qi flow smoothly with fragrance and run counter with stench), which is the reasoning for this prohibition and is retained here as context.

unclassified: 「हिङ्गूष्णं पाचनं रुच्यं तीक्ष्णं वातबलासनुत् / शूलगुल्मोदरानाहकृमिघ्नं पित्तवर्द्धनम् १०१」 (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, हरीतक्यादिवर्गः, v. 101) — REASON: पित्तवर्द्धनम् ("increases pitta") is the closing word of the SAME verse that lists the virtues (hot, digestive, appetising, sharp, destroys vata and kapha, kills colic/gulma/abdominal distension/worms). It is a stated GUNA (property), not a prohibition: the text nowhere says to avoid the drug in pitta conditions. Treating it as a clinical contraindication would require an inference the source does not make, so it is filed here rather than invented into a warning bucket. Flag for a Sanskritist/clinical reviewer to decide whether it should be surfaced as a caution.
