report:
# Load verdict: classical contraindications decomposition

## 1. What is safe to load

All 66 herbs were audited, not a sample. The four slices cover 18 + 24 + 23 + 1 = 66 records, checked line by line against `harvest_verification_results.json` and `eastern_qc_pre1900_results.json`.

| Bucket | Rows | Findings | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| dietary_avoidances | 24 | 0 | **Load.** Not one finding in any slice, in either direction. |
| positive_pairings | 79 | 1 fix, 3 cosmetic | **Load after one character fix** (H214 伏水 → 伏汞). |
| clinical_contraindications | 108 | 3 fix, 1 cosmetic | **Hold.** Three named herbs, all small. |
| drug_incompatibilities | 83 | 4 fix, 4 cosmetic | **Hold.** The most defective bucket. |
| unclassified | 118 | n/a | **Not a field.** Review queue, must not render. |

Blockers, named:

**drug_incompatibilities** carries two rows on H283 (栝蔞) that would actively mislead. One quotes goji as gua lou's *envoy* from inside the incompatibility field, so a helper reads as a hazard. The other imports aconite's reciprocal entry whole, which drags 半夏, 貝母, 白蘞 and 白芨 into gua lou's avoid list, four substances that are not gua lou's antagonists at all. Separately, H142 (黃芩) still renders 辰丹砂 as though 辰 were part of a drug name, and the corrective 1799 witness now sits beside it with a different relation verb and nothing telling the loader which wins. And H274 (天麻) had its single most safety-bearing clause, the 御風草 co-use prohibition with 腸結 as the named harm, moved out of this bucket into unclassified on a schema technicality. Nothing was deleted, but if unclassified does not load, a real prohibition vanishes.

**clinical_contraindications** has three. H002 (黃耆) carries a formula-scoped line restricting *cooling drugs* as though it were a contraindication of a warm herb. H215 (黨參) kept a whole page run intact, so a qualified benefit statement now leads a row under a contraindication heading. H206 (茜草) is the one genuine hole: the BCGM adulterant warning, red-willow root looks identical and taking it causes cataract, is in no bucket at all, not even unclassified, even though the same pass filed the parallel H169 adulterant clauses correctly.

**positive_pairings** has one real error and it is cosmetic in direction but not in appearance: 伏汞 (subdues mercury) was reduced to 伏水, which makes the sentence nonsense. It is inherited from the harvest file, so the upstream string needs correcting too, not just the filing.

## 2. Did the two known failures recur

**Multi-record splitting: fixed.** 13 of 13 expected multi-record herbs merged into single objects. Every herb the brief named as a prior loss was checked clause by clause and is whole: H257 carries all six clinical clauses plus all three 忌鯉魚 rows, H214 carries the full four-limb 火衰/精冷/真元不足/年高之人 list including the age limb that trims easily off a long run, H270's three-item list is complete, H271's three-item prohibition is intact and split into three rows. Two clauses the harvest itself had dropped were recovered (H022, H278). One genuine omission survives (H206, above) and one minor one (H107's 綠豆 pairing, a mitigating relation, so no safety consequence).

**Positive relations filed as warnings: not recurred at the relation level.** Every 使 envoy, every 殺X毒, every 勝 and 解毒 and 制 and 伏 is in positive_pairings across all four slices. The schema fix worked. Two residues remain, both structural rather than a return of the old failure: the H283 composite rows described above, where an envoy is quoted *inside* an incompatibility row, and H215, where a positive clause sits inside a clinical row because the record was kept whole. Both are misfiling of a fragment, not a whole relation pointed the wrong way.

One thing to be plain about: 18 findings on 66 herbs is not a clean run. It is a run whose remaining errors are mostly in the safe direction.

## 3. Was splitting the field the right call

Of 412 rows that all sat in one field labelled "classical contraindications":

| What it actually is | Rows | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Clinical contraindication | 108 | 26% |
| Drug incompatibility | 83 | 20% |
| **Positive pairing** | **79** | **19%** |
| Food lore | 24 | 6% |
| Needs a human | 118 | 29% |

Roughly a quarter of a field called "contraindications" is a contraindication. Counting only rows that got a firm label, it is 37%.

The number that matters is 79. Nearly one row in five in a field displayed to customers as a warning is a statement that two substances *should* be used together, or that one *neutralises* the other's toxicity. 苦參 subdues orpiment. 何首烏 with 地黃 subdues cinnabar. 遠志 kills aconite's toxin. Displayed unsplit, each of those tells a reader to avoid exactly the combination classical practice recommends, which is the precise inversion of the source. Under the original schema, which listed 殺 as a kind of incompatibility, that is where they were headed.

## 4. What positive_pairings is worth alone

79 rows across 66 herbs, in three families: envoy relations (X 為之使, the herb that directs or potentiates), toxicity-neutralising partners (殺, 勝, 解毒), and subduing or restraining pairs (制, 伏). Attested examples include 玄參 as envoy to 苦參 across three separate witnesses, 茯苓 to 何首烏, 紫芝 to 薯蕷, 防風 and 地榆 to their herb, plus 殺附子毒, 制雄黄, 伏硫黄, 伏砒, 解巴豆毒, 勝烏頭, and one recommended food pairing (宜橘皮) that sat immediately beside a 忌鯉魚 prohibition in the same two works and would have been swept negative by proximity alone.

Is it enough to be useful. Yes, with a caveat. 79 rows is thin as coverage (it averages a bit over one per herb and the distribution is uneven, some herbs have none and that is correct, H215 genuinely has no 七情 relations in its source). But it is enough to stand up a real feature: a "traditionally paired with" layer on monographs, an antidote and mitigation view, and a formulation-logic surface that has no Western herbal equivalent because Western sources do not encode drug-to-drug relations this way. It is also fully cited, every row carries its witness and speaker, which is what makes it defensible in customer-facing copy.

Two housekeeping notes before it is worth much: H139's 蒸食消酒毒 is an indication (it dispels wine toxin *in the drinker*), not a drug relation, and filing it here creates a pairing row implying 酒 is a partner drug. And H268's antidotal list reads two drugs in one internal file and three in another; the filed version follows the stronger evidence, but the two files should be reconciled rather than silently chosen between.

## 5. What is still unclassified or unknown

118 rows, the largest bucket, and it is doing real work rather than being a dumping ground. It holds verified absences with the evidence of absence recorded (H177, H261, H035, where a fabricated 1848 quote was previously carried and the honest finding is that the pre-1900 record is silent), textual lacunae preserved verbatim rather than guessed at, formula-scoped lines that must not become herb-level warnings, equipment rules such as 鐵器, variant readings, and one countervailing opinion where 汪昂 in 1694 explicitly rejects a contraindication that two other sources assert. That last one is deliberately not filed either way.

The honest problems:

Three pregnancy signals are parked in unclassified as direction-uncertain (H139 生者墮胎, H253 杀蛔堕胎, H271 通經堕胎). In each case the verified harvest counted the clause as a contraindication. So a signal the verification step graded as a warning currently reaches no safety field. It is escalated with a reason, not silently dropped, but two sources disagree and a person has to rule before this loads.

What is genuinely unknown: whether unclassified has any load destination at all, which determines whether H274's prohibition is merely delayed or lost. Whether the deduplication step is broken more widely, since the byte-identical duplicate rows on H272 and H284 look upstream and only two slices were checked for it. Whether H253's simplified-character transcription matches a woodblock scan, which was flagged as a lead rather than a citation. And the H281 「畏萆。」 truncation is in the 1757 printing itself, so it is a source defect this project inherits, not one it introduced, and it names no substance a lookup key can match.

Recommended sequence: fix the ten items, re-run the audit on the touched herbs only, then decide bucket by bucket. dietary and positive can be settled first; the other two need the H283, H142, H274, H002, H215 and H206 calls made by a human first.
